historical_references.reference: Nagas were a class of divine, semi-divine and demonic serpent beings in Hinduism. The Nagas are often depicted as having the ability to change their forms and shapes, and are associated with water, and the fertility of the earth.

The Naga King, Takshaka, is mentioned in Mahabharata as having the ability to control poison and is considered to be a friend of the Pandava prince, Bhima. He poisons the Kaurava prince, Dushasana, in retaliation for his attack on a Naga queen.
